You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Question: According to the manual of the MA STAR two-post lift, within what maximum interval must the spindle lubrication felt be replaced?

Passages:
[0] mastar-manual, p. 31 — rank: manufacturer's manual
7.2.2 Lubricating the Spindle and the Load Nut A B D C A Oil pan B Lubrication felt C Torx screw D Spindle NOTICE If there is dirt in the oil pan, this can impair the running characteristics of the lift! The oil pan in the lifting carriage must always be filled so that there is a perma- nent lubricating film on the spindle and thermal load is avoided. Refill the oil pan or more often if necessary. Also check the lubrication felt for wear and/or contamination and replace at least every 12 months. The lubrication felt must be positioned at the spindle with its edge facing downward (see illustration). BA364501-en 31

8 Extended Warranty MAHA grants the operator of the lift a warranty on the functionality of the spindle drive beyond the statutory warranty period. This warranty covers wear of the support nut, if it exceeds 2 mm, and wear on the lifting screw, if it restricts / hinders / prevents the operation of the lift. This warranty is limited to the replacement of the worn component(s). It is valid for a maximum of five years after initial start-up and only if the regular inspection and maintenance intervals according to these operating instructions have been demonstrably observed. Compliance is only deemed to have been demonstrated if the required work has been carried out by our factory customer service, one of our dealers or one of our service partners. The extended warranty does not apply if the equipment has not been operated - even temporarily - in accordance with its intended use. 9 Decommissioning, Dismantling and Disposal The device may only be taken out of operation and disassembled by specially authorised and trained personnel. Such specialist staff include authorised, trained specialists employed by the manufacturer, the authorised dealers and the relevant service partners. Observe the product and safety data sheets of the lubricants used. Avoid environmental damage. If the device is to be disposed of, it must be disposed of in an environmentally responsible manner in accordance with local legislation. Sort all dismantled materials according to type and take them to a suitable recycling point. Collect operating materials such as grease, oil, coolant, cleaning fluids containing solvents etc. in suitable containers and dispose of them in an environmentally responsible manner. Alternatively, you can take your device to a waste management company. They will ensure that all parts and fluids are disposed of properly and ecologically. 10 Declaration of Conformity See following page(s). 36 BA364501-en

[10] unict-guideline, p. 2 — rank: company procedure
DEFINIZIONE DI MANUTENZIONE È l’insieme delle operazioni atte a mantenere o a ripristinare le condizioni di corretto funzionamento delle attrezzature. Gli scopi fondamentali della manutenzione sono:  mantenere le macchine e le attrezzature in grado di funzionare nelle condizioni stabilite dal costruttore;  garantire la sicurezza degli operatori e la tutela ambientale;  prolungare la vita utile delle attrezzature;  prevenire i guasti al fine di evitare di intervenire successivamente. Gli interventi di manutenzione possono essere classificati nel seguente modo: - manutenzione ordinaria e preventiva: effettuata indipendentemente dalla comparsa di un guasto, attuata mediante controlli, verifiche, ispezioni e sostituzioni, ad intervalli di tempo prestabiliti e secondo criteri prefissati, ed ha l’obiettivo di evitare che i componenti di un determinato macchinario vengano portati al limite. Generalmente si traduce nell’esecuzione delle procedure specificate nel Manuale d’Uso e Manutenzione del costruttore dell’apparecchiatura e che, generalmente, possono essere eseguite anche dall’operatore. Rientrano nella manutenzione ordinaria, a titolo esemplificativo, le attività di lubrificazione e regolazione di componenti, la sostituzione di utensili e di componenti logori soggetti ad usura, il rabbocco di liquidi, i controlli ordinari di funzionamento sui dispositivi di sicurezza. - manutenzione straordinaria: interventi solitamente eseguiti in seguito al verificarsi di inconvenienti non prevedibili (ad esempio guasti, anomalie, ecc.) e che normalmente sono effettuati da tecnici specializzati. È volta a ripristinare le condizioni di funzionamento iniziali. Tutte le attività di manutenzione, necessarie per garantire nel tempo il permanere delle condizioni di sicurezza dei lavoratori, necessitano della registrazione dei controlli effettuati e dei loro esiti, anche al fine di consentire l’individuazione delle azioni correttive da adottare. Tutte le operazioni devono essere effettuate in condizioni di sicurezza per i lavoratori. Le situazioni non conformi devono essere comunicate attraverso la scala gerarchica al datore di lavoro affinché possa provvedere al ripristino delle condizioni di sicurezza. Qualora la non conformità sia di pregiudizio per la sicurezza dei lavoratori, la macchina non potrà essere utilizzata fino all’adozione delle misure necessarie atte ad eliminar
